hint: recursively shuffle the first n-1 elements, then append element n and swap it into a uniformly random position in [0, n-1]. This is the recursive form of the Fisher-Yates shuffle. Because the result is randomized, the tests below assert invariants (the output is a permutation of the input deck of the correct length) rather than any fixed ordering. Examples: shuffle(0) -> [] shuffle(1) -> [1] sorted(shuffle(5)) -> [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
